label: Quick Actions
title: Start the right agent with the right context.
description: Open the command palette, compose a free prompt, choose the agent, model, permissions, and reasoning, then launch an inspected Session in seconds.
steps: Open Quick Action with Shift Shift.
Describe the change and choose the agent settings.
Launch a Session with the context attached.

label: Task Worktrees
title: Isolation when the task needs it.
description: Create a Task first, then provision one managed worktree when implementation should happen on its own branch. The Task stays useful even without a checkout.
steps: Create a Task for one focused change.
Give the Task its own branch and managed worktree.
Keep parallel changes in separate checkouts.

label: Dev Server
title: Define it once. Start it where you work.
description: Save a Project dev-server command and fallback URL, then launch the real process from the Project or its Task worktrees. Its terminal and discovered URLs stay visible.
steps: Save a preview command for the Project.
Start the command in the checkout you are using.
Follow the process output and discovered preview URL.

label: Multi-Agent
title: One workspace. Several live agents.
description: Run multiple Claude and Codex Sessions across tasks and worktrees. See who is active, which checkout changed, and which terminal needs attention.
steps: Keep several agent Sessions in one Project.
Use the sidebar to see which Session needs attention.
Open the right terminal without losing the other Sessions.

label: Ask To
title: Get a second opinion without copy-paste.
description: Ask one agent to consult another agent. TermLoop creates a visible helper Session, preserves the relationship, and returns the answer to the requester.
steps: Open Agents > Ask to and choose a provider for the second opinion.
A visible helper Session receives the question and context.
The answer returns to the requesting agent.
provenance: OBS Studio · Launchpad Demo · continuous 30 FPS recording

label: Handoff
title: Move context to the agent already in the work.
description: Send a visible, composed handoff from one running Project Session to another. The target receives the brief in its own real terminal and continues from there.
steps: Open Agents > Handover to and choose an existing Session.
The current agent composes the request, findings, and next action.
The destination receives the handoff in its own terminal.
provenance: OBS Studio · Launchpad Demo · continuous 30 FPS recording

label: Session Fork
title: Explore another direction in a real terminal.
description: Fork a Session from the sidebar, see the parent-child relationship, and continue in a new Ghostty terminal. The branch in thinking is explicit instead of becoming another anonymous tab.
steps: Choose a conversation to explore in a new direction.
Fork it from the Session menu.
Continue in a separate Session with visible parentage.
provenance: OBS Studio · Launchpad Demo · continuous 30 FPS recording

label: Changes
title: Review the diff where the work happened.
description: Changed-file counts appear on Tasks and active Agents. Open the Git changes view, inspect the real diff, and leave line-level notes for the agent to address.
steps: Open the changed files for the checkout.
Read the diff and attach a note to a relevant line.
Send review notes to the selected active agent.

label: Task Lifecycle
title: Close the work without erasing it.
description: Tasks have a deliberately small lifecycle: open or closed. Close finished work, keep its current state visible, and reopen it when the next change arrives.
steps: Close a Task when the work is finished.
Keep completed work in the Closed section.
Reopen the Task when another change is needed.

label: Session Refresh
title: Refresh the display, not the identity.
description: Recover a stale agent display from the Session menu while keeping the same durable Session and process model. Lifecycle actions remain explicit.
steps: Open the Session actions menu.
Refresh the provider display for the same conversation.
Return to the durable Session after the display restarts.

label: Steward
title: A Project-scoped operator that stays present.
description: Ask the persistent Steward what should ship next, let it coordinate Tasks and Sessions through its constrained tools, and keep the conversation attached to the Project.
steps: Open the Project Steward workspace.
Keep project-level instructions beside the work.
Coordinate Tasks through a persistent Project assistant.

label: Mobile Companion
title: Check the loop when you leave the desk.
description: Pair your phone, keep Project visibility and terminal input scoped to your computer, and follow long-running agents over your trusted network.
steps: Open Connect Mobile from the desktop.
Use the pairing flow on your trusted network.
Continue with project visibility and terminal input on your phone.

label: Mcp & Prompts
title: Inspect the tools and instructions agents receive.
description: Browse role-scoped MCP tools and the built-in prompt catalog. TermLoop-generated instructions remain visible and editable; provider-managed opaque layers are labeled honestly.
steps: Open the tools and prompt libraries.
Read the instructions and tool descriptions agents receive.
Keep TermLoop-authored context inspectable.

label: Task briefs
title: Start with a clear definition of done.
description: Give each Task a title, a focused brief, and acceptance criteria. Open its detail view to keep the goal beside Sessions and checkout state.
steps: Open the onboarding Task from the sidebar.
Read its brief and concrete acceptance criteria.
Keep the goal attached to the work as the Task evolves.

label: Run configurations
title: Keep launch commands with the Project.
description: Save named commands for preview servers, tests, and other local processes. Configure setup commands and fallback URLs in the same editor.
steps: Open the saved Launchpad preview configuration.
Review pnpm dev, the setup command, and fallback URL.
Reuse the configuration when starting work in a checkout.

label: Agent library
title: Choose a specialist for the next question.
description: Browse reusable agent profiles with a defined purpose. Inspect their provider, working mode, reasoning, and instructions before running one.
steps: Open the Agents library.
Inspect the Edge Case Hunter profile and its working mode.
Choose a profile whose instructions match the task.

label: Custom agents
title: Save the reviewer your team actually needs.
description: Create a reusable agent with its own name, provider settings, and instructions. The Launchpad example checks progress bounds, tests, and keyboard accessibility.
steps: Open your saved Launchpad reviewer profile.
Give the Launchpad reviewer focused, project-specific instructions.
Save the profile so the same brief can be used again.

label: Workflow templates
title: Make the collaboration repeatable.
description: Define discussion, implementation, review, and fix steps in a Project template. Choose the agent conversation and instructions for each step before running it in a ready Task worktree.
steps: Open the saved Discuss, build, review template.
Inspect the ordered discussion, implementation, and review steps.
Reuse the template for the next Task with a ready worktree.

label: Review cycles
title: Give review a clear stopping rule.
description: Configure review and fix steps together, including a maximum number of review rounds. The template makes the review instructions and return path visible.
steps: Select the accessibility and tests review step.
Give the reviewer a specific checklist to assess.
Bound the fix-and-review cycle with a maximum round count.

label: Developer notes
title: Keep small follow-ups beside the Task.
description: Turn the human checks around a change into a short checklist. Mark individual notes complete while keeping their context visible in the sidebar.
steps: Start with the onboarding Task and its three checks.
Mark the completed tests and keyboard check as done.
See the checklist reach three of three without leaving the Task.

label: Task favorites
title: Keep important work easy to recognize.
description: Mark a Task as a favorite directly from its row. The explicit favorite state lets you distinguish priority work from the rest of the Project.
steps: Reveal the actions on the onboarding Task.
Toggle the Task favorite with its star control.
Keep the Task marked while its notes and brief stay intact.

label: Full-file review
title: Read the context around the diff.
description: Switch from changed lines to the whole file when more context helps. Use unified or split comparison to inspect the same checkout changes.
steps: Open the actual changes in src/releases.mjs.
Switch from Change focus to Full file.
Choose Split to compare the old and new versions side by side.

label: Review progress
title: Remember which files you have checked.
description: Mark changed files as reviewed as you work through the diff. A visible counter shows what remains in the current review.
steps: Start with two changed files in the Launchpad checkout.
Mark each file after inspecting its changes.
See two of two reviewed before returning to the Task.

label: Task archive
title: Park context without deleting the Task.
description: Use the archive preview to inspect whether a Task can be parked safely. Eligible Tasks move out of active work and remain available in Archived items.
steps: Choose Archive Task from the Task actions.
Read the archive preview before confirming.
The Task moves out of the active list and into the archive.

label: Restore archived work
title: Bring a parked Task back into the Project.
description: Expand Archived items and restore the Task when work resumes. Its brief and developer notes return with it; eligible agent recovery follows the archive restore flow.
steps: Expand Archived items to find the onboarding Task.
Restore the Task from its archived row.
Its brief and completed developer notes return to active work.

label: Pause to read
title: Read output while the Session keeps running.
description: Pause the terminal display to inspect output at your own pace. Return to live when you are ready; pausing the view does not stop the process.
steps: Run the five real Launchpad release tests.
Use Pause to read to hold the displayed output.
Return to live without ending the Session.

label: Keep Awake
title: Give long-running work time to finish.
description: Choose whether to keep the computer awake while agents run, continuously, or for a limited time. Keeping the display on is a separate option.
steps: Open Keep Awake from the sidebar.
Compare Off, While agents run, and Always.
Use a timer or the separate display option when needed.

label: Notification preferences
title: Choose when each device should alert you.
description: Configure desktop, iPhone, and Apple Watch notification preferences. Separate input requests, review-ready alerts, and Steward messages by device.
steps: Open Settings and choose Notifications.
Review alerts for agent input, completed turns, and Steward messages.
Choose device-specific sound and active-computer behavior.

label: Appearance
title: Match the workspace to your environment.
description: Choose Light, Dark, or System appearance. The resolved theme applies to the app and terminal panes, with System following the computer preference.
steps: Open Appearance in Settings.
Compare the Light and Dark workspace themes.
Choose System to follow the computer automatically.

label: Context Bank
title: See the instructions in your checkout.
description: Browse project and folder-level instruction files in a searchable tree. Open the real file, inspect its contents, and see its recommended line budget.
steps: Open Context for the Launchpad Project.
Read the root instructions, then the source-folder instructions.
Use the file path and line budget to keep context focused.

label: Instruction consistency
title: Resolve conflicting sibling instructions explicitly.
description: Context Bank flags differing sibling instruction files such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Choose the source of truth and review the overwrite count before applying it.
steps: Rescan after sibling instruction files change.
Compare the source choices in the conflict resolver.
Choose the source file and apply the explicit synchronization.

label: Skill library
title: Find and inspect reusable skills.
description: Search discovered skills and open their actual instructions. The library shows their locations and provider deployment state so you can understand what is installed.
steps: Search the skill library for simplify.
Open the skill and read its instructions in the editor.
Inspect its discovered locations and provider installation state.
